evidence.curator_note: First alpha-cleavage (ring opening) of the stepwise retro-Diels-Alder of a 4-R-cyclohexene molecular ion - the SAME ring-opening step shared with eq 4.31; the book draws it once (top row of p.70) and the ring-opened distonic radical cation is the common branch point marked with the '|||' (identical-structure) sign between eqs 4.31 and 4.32. ARC COUNT: the book draws 3 arc(s) and all three are printed - a fully drawn 3-fishhook alpha-cleavage. Move <1> (top-right fishhook next to the dot) = the odd electron on the pi-ionized alkene carbon (map 6) into the forming C6=C7 pi bond; move <2> (large central arc across the top of the ring) = one electron of the breaking C2-C7 ring sigma bond into that same forming pi bond; move <3> (small top-left fishhook next to R) = the other electron of the C2-C7 bond onto the R-bearing carbon (map 2). LOCALIZATION (convention B/C): the alkene radical cation is drawn localized as C5(+)-C6(.) (cation map 5, odd electron map 6); the neutral C=C sat between maps 5 and 6. Instantiated as R=C6H5 (4-phenylcyclohexene), map 1 = phenyl ipso carbon.

locator.section: 4 / Basic Mechanisms of Ion Fragmentation (retro-Diels-Alder, charge migration)

evidence.curator_note: Inductive (charge-migration) cleavage on the same ring-opened distonic radical cation (eq 4.32, arrow labelled 'i'): the C5(+) charge induces heterolytic cleavage of the C3-C4 bond, both electrons flowing into the new C4=C5 pi bond. ARC COUNT: the book draws 1 arc - a single double-barbed (full arrowhead) curved arrow at the bottom of the intermediate, from the C3-C4 bond sweeping toward the cation. Move <1> (electron_count 2) fully accounts for the step: the map3-map4 bond is broken heterolytically and the map4-map5 bond gains one order, so no implicit hook is needed. Charge MIGRATES from map 5 to map 3: the R-bearing fragment (Ph-CH(.)-CH2(+), the styrene radical cation, m/z 104) keeps the charge and neutral 1,3-butadiene (maps 4-7) leaves. PRINTED INTENSITIES for the R-fragment ion: R=H <5% (IE 10.5); R=C6H5 100% (IE of the styrene fragment 8.4). This record instantiates R=C6H5, hence relative_intensity 1.0 - m/z 104 is the base peak of 4-phenylcyclohexene, phenyl stabilising the migrated charge.

Cross-linked to MOD rules IMS_4_32_alpha and IMS_4_32_ind. VERIFIED against their DFS. IMS_4_32_alpha '[C]1[C]2[C]3[C]4[C+]5[C.]6[C]7{-}2>>[C]1[C.]2[C]3[C]4[C+]5[C]6{=}[C]7' is BYTE-IDENTICAL to IMS_4_31_alpha1 - the shared ring-opening first alpha cleavage (step_alpha1_ring_opening); it breaks ring bond map2-map7, forms C6=C7 and moves the radical map6->map2. IMS_4_32_ind '[C]1[C.]2[C]3[C]4[C+]5[C]6{=}[C]7>>[C]1[C.]2[C+]3.[C]4{=}[C]5[C]6{=}[C]7' cleaves map3-map4, forms the C4=C5 pi bond and moves the charge from map5 to map3 while the radical stays on map2 - exactly step_inductive_charge_migration; the products are the [C.]2[C+]3 R-fragment radical cation (charge retained on the phenyl-bearing map1/2/3 fragment) plus neutral butadiene [C]4{=}[C]5[C]6{=}[C]7. The cleaved map3-map4 bond is incident to map4, which forms the new C4=C5 bond, so the inductive rule is correctly encoded (no mismatch). R=C6H5 instantiation as in eq 4.31 (map1 = phenyl ipso); the generic rules use a bare carbon handle at map1.
